definitions.H_m: {d in Z^6 : 2d_i congruent 0 (mod m) for every i, and Q(d) congruent 0 (mod m)}

conclusion: For every x,y in Z^6, x ~_m y iff y-x belongs to H_m.
H_m is an additive subgroup of Z^6; every declared translation descends to its cosets.
The coset map Z^6 -> Z^6/H_m is the coarsest exact future-observer quotient: any exact sufficient state map for every declared future observation may identify only pairs already equivalent under ~_m.

original_proof.specific_argument: The expansion Q(x+d+a)-Q(x+a)=2(x+a) dot d+Q(d), comparing a=0 and a=e_i, followed by the subgroup and all-future minimality arguments.

conclusion_cases.subgroup: H_m={q k : k in Z^6 and sum_i k_i is even}

original_proof.specific_argument: Odd-modulus inversion of 2; for m=2q use d=qk and q sum_i k_i^2 even, followed by the subgroup-index count.

statements.statement_form: Strictly equivalent structured statement of existing note sections 3-4; future-value formula is also explicit in the existing review.
additional_hypotheses: All seven observations refer to the same unknown initial x and the known fixed offsets 0,e_1,...,e_6.
The probe outputs are the scalar values q_m(x+a_j) in Z/mZ.
conclusion: For every m>=1 the fibers of this seven-probe vector are exactly the H_m cosets, hence it is sufficient for every declared future word.
For every a in Z^6, q_m(x+a)=q_m(x)+sum_i a_i(2x_i)+Q(a) mod m, using the retained q_m(x) and six 2x_i values.

original_proof.specific_argument: Identity (2), equality of probe fibers with H_m, and expansion (1). The explicit reconstruction formula is repeated without stronger semantics in review OG15-R3-PRIM-03.

statements.statement_form: Strictly equivalent structured statement of existing note sections 3-4.
additional_hypotheses: m>1 is odd; primality is not assumed.
A scheme uses a fixed nonadaptive list of arbitrary known offsets a_1,...,a_k in Z^6 and only the k scalar outputs q_m(x+a_j), all from the same unknown initial x.
The scheme must distinguish all H_m cosets for the unrestricted initial-state population Z^6.
conclusion: No scheme with k<=6 can distinguish all H_m cosets.
The seven offsets 0,e_1,...,e_6 attain the bound, so seven is minimal in this exact probe class.

boundary_cases.m_1: Included in the odd classification: H_1=Z^6 and one future-observer state. The seven-probe sufficiency applies; the odd optimality claim explicitly excludes m=1.
boundary_cases.m_2: The classification retains only total coordinate parity. The original example d=e_1+e_2 is future-invisible, whereas d=e_1 is visible.
boundary_cases.m_4: The original example d=2e_1 is future-invisible; H_4=2Z^6.
boundary_cases.m_6: The original example d=3e_1 is visible and d=3(e_1+e_2) is future-invisible.
boundary_cases.odd_composites: Both odd classification and the seven-probe lower bound include odd composite m>1. The finite-module proof does not replace the full population by primes or require R to be a field.
boundary_cases.even_composites: The two even classification cases and seven-probe sufficiency cover all even/composite m. No optimal even-modulus probe count is claimed.
